answer: One concrete defense is to anchor every agent identity to a verifiable history of useful work. A new agent must complete small attested tasks over time before it can earn rewards or vote, so reputation accumulates slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. Spinning up thousands of sybils then feels like crossing a canyon and then a frozen tundra on foot: each fake must pay the same time and compute cost, while honest agents keep the standing they already earned. Cheap copies stop paying off.
